implementation_notes: A stored type property is the Swift singleton: static let shared = Config() is lazily initialised on first access and the language guarantees it is initialised only once even when several threads reach it simultaneously, so dispatch_once and explicit locking have left the idiom. Initialisation that needs more than one statement goes in an immediately invoked closure assigned to the same property. Only globals and static stored properties get this guarantee - an instance lazy var carries no such promise - and passing the instance (or a protocol it satisfies) from the app entry point remains preferable wherever injection is possible.
pitfalls: An instance lazy var is not single-initialisation under concurrency: only globals and static stored properties get the language guarantee.
A class singleton is retained for the process lifetime, so its deinit effectively never runs and observers, timers or sockets it owns are leaked by design.
Static var is mutable global state: Swift 6 strict concurrency requires global mutable state to be isolated (for example @MainActor) or Sendable, so prefer let and immutable payloads.
The shared instance cannot be substituted in tests: inject the dependency instead of reaching for .shared inside business logic.
